clue.text: Poet's leading principle almost to settle for a town

parts.note: John Milton wrote Paradise Lost; the possessive adds no letter
a key idea or principle is the one that leads the rest

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: birds settle when they nest

explanation.surface: A poet's guiding principle is nearly enough to make him settle down in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of NEST to leave NES. MILTON KEYNES is a new town in Buckinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Keynes is a large planned settlement in Buckinghamshire, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Long time not observed on the calendar

definitions.text: Long time not observed on the calendar

parts.words: Long time not observed on the calendar
parts.note: an idiom for a very long period, read cryptically as a stretch of weeks of rest days that no calendar ever shows

explanation.surface: A very long time that no calendar records.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an extremely long while; a period made only of Sabbath days never appears in any real calendar.

clue.text: Shocking line-SOs, There's something out of the zoo!

indicators.note: shocking suggests letters jolted into disorder, so the following fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: A startled exclamation about some shocking line of distress calls, as if a beast had escaped from the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' rearranges the seven letters of LINESOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cat is a typical zoo animal, so a female of that species is something you might see there.

clue.text: It could be in Albert Hall before artist takes in box

definitions.text: It could be in Albert Hall

indicators.note: takes in means one piece swallows another, so the box sits inside the two other pieces

parts.note: or is an old poetic word for before (or ever)
RA is a Royal Academician, a standard abbreviation for an artist
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: Something might be found in the Albert Hall before an artist takes a box seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' is the container signal. The Royal Albert Hall is a London concert venue, home of the Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: Symphonic players regularly perform at that concert hall, so a band of them is an example of what you could find there.

clue.text: See 1
Delete periods of time at end of game

parts.note: eras are long periods of time

indicators.note: end of means take only the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Wiping the game clock clean at the final whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out something written is to remove it, the same as deleting it.

clue.text: Harmful omen is nothing when unreliable

indicators.note: unreliable letters cannot be trusted to stay in order, so the fodder is rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A bad omen means nothing when it is not reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious and offensive things are harmful or unpleasant, the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Hunting for scorch I feature on top of grate

parts.note: to sear is to scorch
the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: top of means take only the first letter of the following word in this down clue

explanation.surface: Searching for a burnt mark on the top of a fireplace grate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on top of' places CHIN above G, the first letter of 'grate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching means seeking or looking for something, the same activity as hunting.

clue.text: Where some kickers put the ball, keeping up with things

definitions.text: Where some kickers put the ball
definitions.meaning: in rugby a kick that sends the ball over the sideline puts it out of play beyond the touchline
staying informed and up to date

explanation.walkthrough: Rugby players often kick for touch, sending the ball over the sideline to gain ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, the area beyond the sidelines is called touch; being informed about current events is also said this way.

clue.text: Bill's character can include a politician

indicators.note: include means the outer word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A tin that holds a politician as one of the characters in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' is the container signal. 'Bill' is William Shakespeare; Caliban is the creature in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: The monstrous slave in The Tempest is a figure in one of Shakespeare's plays, so he is that playwright's creation.

clue.text: It could be part of the cycle

definitions.text: It could be part of the cycle

parts.words: It could be part of the cycle
parts.note: reads like a stage in a sequence or series, but means a fitting on a bicycle

explanation.surface: Something forms one stage of a repeating sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier pouch hangs behind a bike seat, making it literally a component of a bicycle.

clue.text: Seek Eastern cache in secret last course?

indicators.note: kept in secret, the letters are disguised by being reordered

explanation.surface: Hunting for a hidden Oriental store of treasure as a final adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy baked dessert is often served at the end of a meal, so it can be the final course; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Sense (not with head) expression of pain

indicators.note: not with head means drop the first letter of the word

parts.note: touch is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Senseless and headless, one can only cry out in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not with head' removes the T from TOUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the exclamation people utter when hurt, so it voices pain.

clue.text: Stone broken for an attack

indicators.note: a broken stone falls into pieces, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stone smashed to pieces as part of an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of an assault or a sudden onslaught is a classic sense of the word.

clue.text: See 1 down
The old could be doing P.E. with credit

indicators.note: doing in the sense of working over or manipulating the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Old people may be gym class pupils earning credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing' rearranges PE + CREDIT; P.E. is physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly people are sometimes described as worn out and frail with age.

clue.text: See 25 across
Pronounce aitches e.g. like Hook?

parts.note: as means like
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Dropping or sounding one's aitches like Captain Hook would.
explanation.walkthrough: To aspirate is to sound the h at the start of a word; Hook is the villain of Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetics uses the verb for giving a breathy h sound, so it means sounding the letter h.

clue.text: Examine hotels worked on by beak (it is said)

indicators.note: it is said signals that the words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: inns are hotels and pecked means worked on by a beak

explanation.surface: Hotels being attacked by a bird's beak, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise or check something closely is to examine it.

clue.text: Dishonest way of resting

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the verb: telling falsehoods, and reclining horizontally.

clue.text: Put 'em in one site, collected together make a list

indicators.note: gathered up and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Gather them all on one site, then draw up an inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: To list things one by one is to set them out item by item.

clue.text: The burden concerning America?

parts.note: on means about or concerning
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Asking whether the responsibility falls on America.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty or responsibility that someone must bear is a burden.

clue.text: She could get such a fee with fun mainly getting around

indicators.note: getting around suggests letters moved about, so the fodder is rearranged
mainly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

explanation.surface: A woman might earn such a fee with mostly fun driving around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter, leaving FU; 'getting around' is the anagram signal. A chauffeuse is a woman chauffeur.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the feminine form of a paid driver, so the person is a woman.

clue.text: Chocolate source

parts.note: the plant whose beans give cocoa

explanation.definitionFit: The bean of this tropical tree is roasted and ground to make cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Enclose in street, exhausted

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to pen is to enclose

explanation.surface: Fencing in a street leaves everyone worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being used up or drained of energy is to be exhausted.

clue.text: Beat rotter in French church

parts.note: a cad is a rotter
en is French for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Thrashing a scoundrel inside a church in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhythm or metre in music or verse is a beat.

clue.text: Jeers at path within Education Department

indicators.note: within puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: DES was the Department of Education and Science
a ride is a path through woodland

explanation.surface: Mocking a route through the education ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' is the container signal. DES was the former UK Department of Education and Science; a ride is a track for horse riding.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or ridicule someone is to jeer at them.

clue.text: Down Midland town with London borough about ancient region

parts.note: Sutton is a borough in south London
c is circa, about
old means ancient
a field is an area or region of activity

explanation.surface: A trip down to a Midlands town with a London borough near some ancient area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' points to 15 down, the rest of this answer. Sutton Coldfield is a town near Birmingham in England's Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutton Coldfield is a royal town in the West Midlands, north of Birmingham.

clue.text: Announcement: opening coming

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement or announcement
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A notice declares that an opening is about to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an arrival or coming into being, as of a new era.
